title: Approximate a closed subscheme missing one fibre over an affine base
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $g:T\to S$ be any scheme morphism, and let $t\in T$. Write $X_T=X\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $Z\hookrightarrow X_T$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] with empty fibre over $t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There exist an affine open neighbourhood $V\subseteq T$ of $t$, nonnegative integers $r,m$, polynomials $q_1,\ldots,q_m\in A[z_1,\ldots,z_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], an affine $S$-scheme $T\prime=\operatorname{Spec}(A[z_1,\ldots,z_r]/(q_1,\ldots,q_m))$, an $S$-morphism $a:V\to T\prime$, and a closed subscheme $Z\prime\hookrightarrow X\times_ST\prime$ such that the fibre of $Z\prime$ over $a(t)$ is empty and the image of $Z\times_TV$ under $X\times_SV\to X\times_ST\prime$ is contained in $Z\prime$. The map $a$ is over $S$, so its composite with $T\prime\to S$ is $g|_V$. No finite-type, Noetherian or separatedness assumption is imposed on $X$, $T$ or $A$.

source.place: Tag 05BD, limits-lemma-separate, specialized to affine S=Spec A; the proof explicitly constructs Tprime=Spec B_lambda with B_lambda a finitely presented A-algebra, yielding the displayed polynomial quotient. This is the approximation input in the proof of Tag 05JX, limits-lemma-test-universally-closed.

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $t$ and replace $Z$ by $Z_V=Z\times_TV$. Write $\mathfrak q\subset B$ for $t$. Since $S$ is affine and $f$ is quasi-compact, $X=f^{-1}(S)$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open] to the open $X$ itself to obtain $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^nU_i$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U_i\times_SV=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ with $R_i=C_i\otimes_AB$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], its inverse image in $Z_V$ is $\operatorname{Spec}D_i$, $D_i=R_i/I_i$ for an ideal $I_i$. Its fibre at $\mathfrak q$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(D_i\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak q))$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and the affine-fibre-product formula. It is empty by hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 05BD, lemma-separate, proof; affine reduction and finite affine cover

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-localization-quotient] to $B\to D_i$ and $\mathfrak q$. The fibre ring is $(B\setminus\mathfrak q)^{-1}D_i/\mathfrak q(B\setminus\mathfrak q)^{-1}D_i$. It is the zero ring: its spectrum is empty by step 1, and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](i), applied to the empty family of basic opens, gives $0=(1)$. Thus $1=\sum_j f_{ij}(d_{ij}/s_{ij})$ in $(B\setminus\mathfrak q)^{-1}D_i$ with finitely many $f_{ij}\in\mathfrak q$, $d_{ij}\in D_i$, $s_{ij}\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$. Put $s_i=\prod_js_{ij}$ and $e_{ij}=d_{ij}\prod_{k\ne j}s_{ik}$. The equality of fractions implies that some $h_i\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ kills $s_i-\sum_jf_{ij}e_{ij}$ in $D_i$, by the fraction equality in the cited node. Lift $h_ie_{ij}$ to $c_{ij}\in R_i$ and put $g_i=h_is_i\notin\mathfrak q$. Then $x_i:=g_i-\sum_jf_{ij}c_{ij}\in I_i$, so $x_i+\sum_jf_{ij}c_{ij}=g_i$ in $R_i$. Empty sums and products cause no exception when $D_i$ is already zero.

source.place: Tag 05BD, lemma-separate, proof; clearing denominators, before the optional localization of B

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-colimit-fp-algebras-over-it] to $A\to B$, taking $\mathcal P$ to be the set of all explicit polynomial quotients $A[z_1,\ldots,z_r]/(q_1,\ldots,q_m)$ for finite $r,m$. It gives a small filtered category $\mathcal I$ of such algebras $B_\lambda$ with compatible maps $\alpha_\lambda:B_\lambda\to B$ and colimit $B$. Work in a common universe large enough for $\mathcal I$ and all these rings and the finitely many $C_i$, as required by the tensor-colimit node used next. This uses the set of presentations, rather than a potentially large category of all algebras.

source.place: Tag 05BD, lemma-separate, proof; write B as a filtered colimit of finitely presented A-algebras

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise](1), first with the $A$-module $N=A$ (identifying $B_\lambda\otimes_AA$ with $B_\lambda$), to lift all $f_{ij},g_i$. Use it with $N=C_i$ to lift $x_i,c_{ij}$ to $C_i\otimes_AB_\lambda$; the switch $b\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes b$ is the tensor symmetry, directly inverse to $c\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes c$. There are only finitely many elements. Repeatedly use the common-target property of the filtered category supplied in step 3 and transport the chosen lifts, obtaining one object $\lambda$ carrying them all. Denote them $x_{i\lambda},c_{ij\lambda},f_{ij\lambda},g_{i\lambda}$. Put $\mathfrak q_\lambda=\alpha_\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; then $f_{ij\lambda}\in\mathfrak q_\lambda$ and $g_{i\lambda}\notin\mathfrak q_\lambda$, simply because their images in $B$ are $f_{ij}$ and $g_i$.

source.place: Tag 05BD, lemma-separate, proof; lift finitely many coefficients and tensor elements

proof.text: The element $x_{i\lambda}+\sum_jf_{ij\lambda}c_{ij\lambda}-g_{i\lambda}$ maps to zero in $C_i\otimes_AB$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise](2), it becomes zero after some arrow out of $\lambda$. Impose these finitely many equations successively: after each arrow the remaining errors still map to zero in the colimit, and all equations already imposed remain zero because transition maps are ring homomorphisms (the same node's last clause). Replacing $\lambda$ by the final object gives $x_{i\lambda}+\sum_jf_{ij\lambda}c_{ij\lambda}=g_{i\lambda}$ for every $i$. All the image and prime-membership conditions of step 4 persist. No injectivity of the stage maps is used.

source.place: Tag 05BD, lemma-separate, proof; increase the stage until the finitely many equations hold

proof.text: Set $T'=\operatorname{Spec}B_\lambda$ and $a=\operatorname{Spec}\alpha_\lambda:V\to T'$. This is over $S$ by functoriality of affine spectra. Since the object $B_\lambda$ was chosen from the explicit polynomial quotients in step 3, it has exactly the displayed presentation in the statement. Let $p:X\times_SV\to X\times_ST'$ be the base change of $a$; it is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1). The map $Z_V\hookrightarrow X\times_SV$ is affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $h:Z_V\to X\times_ST'$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-composition], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel] to define its closed scheme-theoretic image $Z'$. On $U_i\times_ST'=\operatorname{Spec}(C_i\otimes_AB_\lambda)$ the cited kernel formula identifies the ideal $J_i$ of $Z'$ with $\ker(C_i\otimes_AB_\lambda\to D_i)$. Here the inverse image under $h$ is exactly $Z_V\cap(U_i\times_SV)=\operatorname{Spec}D_i$, by the defining projection identities of the fibre product. In particular $x_{i\lambda}\in J_i$.

source.place: Tag 05BD, lemma-separate, proof; take the scheme-theoretic image and compute its ideals on affine pieces

proof.text: The point $a(t)$ is $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ by the contravariant description of affine spectra. In the fibre of $Z'$ on the $i$th chart, $x_{i\lambda}$ vanishes since it belongs to $J_i$, and each $f_{ij\lambda}$ vanishes since it belongs to $\mathfrak q_\lambda$. Step 5 therefore makes $g_{i\lambda}$ zero. But $g_{i\lambda}\notin\mathfrak q_\lambda$, so it is invertible in the residue field of $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and hence in this fibre algebra. That algebra has $1=0$ and its spectrum is empty, since a prime ideal is proper. The affine charts cover $X\times_ST'$, so the whole fibre of $Z'$ is empty. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel] supplies a factorization of $h$ through $Z'$, which implies the required image containment (indeed scheme-theoretic factorization). This proves all clauses, with no condition on affine-open intersections of $X$.

source.place: Tag 05BD, lemma-separate, proof; the descended relation kills each fibre chart and the image factorization gives containment
